summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, iron deficiency anemia, and depression was admitted for worsening fatigue, sharp abdominal pain, and passive suicidal ideation. Her hemoglobin was 8.1 g/dL, consistent with chronic anemia, and she received IV iron with reported improvement in energy. Imaging showed mildly dilated bowel loops but no acute obstruction. A colonoscopy revealed duodenal and rectal ulcers, which were biopsied and treated with sucralfate and increased rabeprazole. Psychiatry evaluated her after expressed passive suicidal thoughts; she improved and was cleared for discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for outpatient GI and psychiatric follow-up, and instructions to monitor for GI bleed symptoms.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
